samples.summary: Vacuous guard: `assert.ok(step.length > 0)` can never fail when mark-ready.mjs is no longer invoked
samples.evidence: `const step = yml.slice(yml.indexOf("node ./scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs"))`. If the string is absent, indexOf returns -1 and `slice(-1)` yields the last character — a 1-char string — so the assertion "the promote job must still invoke mark-ready.mjs" holds regardless. The subsequent `assert.match` calls do catch the removal, so the failure message is just misleading, but the assertion itself is fake coverage. `assert.ok(yml.includes(...))` would be honest.

samples.summary: The 'no exit code outside {0,1,2,3}' test is a literal-only source grep and passes vacuously for any non-literal exit
samples.evidence: `SOURCE.matchAll(/process\.exit\((\d+)\)/g)` only sees integer literals. `process.exit(code)`, `process.exitCode = 4`, `throw` (→ code 1 accidentally), or an exit inside an imported helper are all invisible, so the test would go green while the workflow's `-eq` chain silently falls through to success — precisely the failure the header says it exists to catch. It also never asserts that all four codes are still USED, so deleting the exit-3 path leaves it green (only the yml-branch test would notice, and that test reads the workflow, not the script).

samples.summary: No test asserts the promotion mutations actually use GH_MUTATION_TOKEN, the regression the exit-3 contract exists for
samples.evidence: `ghMutate` (mark-ready.mjs:93-97) exists solely because the default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot markPullRequestReadyForReview and previously left gate-passing PRs stuck as drafts. The stub `gh` logs only `process.argv.slice(2)` (test line 47) and never records `process.env.GH_TOKEN`, and the exit-3 test only matches the literal string /GH_MUTATION_TOKEN/ in the error MESSAGE (line 219). If `ghMutate` silently reverted to plain `gh`/`execFileSync` without the token env, every test in this file stays green. The stub could `appendFileSync(log, joined + " token=" + process.env.GH_TOKEN)` and let the promote test assert `token=stub-app-token`.
searchedFor: grep GH_MUTATION_TOKEN in the new test file and workflow

samples.summary: Gate 1's 'latest CI run for this SHA wins' re-run logic is untested
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` sorts workflow_runs by created_at descending and reads only runs[0].conclusion (mark-ready.mjs:133-137). Every fixture in the new test passes at most ONE workflow run (okConfig line 70, and the three exit-1 cases at lines 138-142), so a broken/removed sort — e.g. an old `success` re-run preceding a newer `failure` — would promote a red PR with all tests green. A two-run fixture (older success + newer failure → exit 1, and the reverse → exit 0) would pin it. checks.mjs's own started_at sort is covered by checks.test.mjs; this created_at sort lives only in mark-ready.mjs and has no test.
searchedFor: scanned new test file for multi-run workflowRuns fixtures

samples.summary: The stale-label race mitigation (re-read labels, fall back to the initial snapshot) is only half tested
samples.evidence: The promote test (test lines 180-192) asserts the PUT contents, but the stub always answers the `pr view … --json labels` re-read from the same cfg.pr.labels as the initial view, so the test cannot distinguish 'labels re-read just before the PUT' from 'labels reused from the stale first read' — the very behavior the comment at mark-ready.mjs:221-224 says was added. Nor is the catch-fallback (`current = pr.labels`) exercised; the stub's prefix matcher could target exactly `pr view 7 --json labels` since the initial call's joined string differs. A cfg allowing different labels for the second view would make this test able to fail.
searchedFor: scanned tests for a second-read fixture

samples.summary: Dry-run test does not assert the label PUT was skipped
samples.evidence: The dry-run test asserts `!promoted(calls)` and no `pr comment`, but never `!calls.some(c => c.startsWith("api -X PUT"))`, so a regression that relabelled the PR without --promote would go unnoticed there (the exit-3 test does assert this for its own path).
